name: Baby Shower
tagline: Advice, guesses and "parent edition" would-you-rathers for the parents-to-be.

cards.text: Share the one piece of advice you'd give {names} for the very first night home.
What's the best thing someone ever did for you (or a friend) after a new baby arrived? Tell {names}.
Give {names} a tip for getting out of the house on time with a little one. Bonus points if it's genuinely useful.
What's one thing {names} should NOT bother buying? Everyone else: nod if you agree.
Share a lullaby, rhyme or bedtime ritual from your own family that {names} could borrow.
In ten words or fewer: your best advice for staying a team when you're both tired.
What's the most useful thing you learned from a grandparent? Pass it on to {names}.
Recommend one small daily ritual {names} should start with the baby from day one.
Guess the baby's first word. Everyone answers at once on three — most popular answer wins!
Whose laugh will the baby have — {name}'s or someone else's in the family? Make your case.
Guess the baby's future favourite food. The most creative answer gets a round of applause.
Predict the baby's first big talent: singing, dancing, drawing, building, or making everyone laugh?
Guess which family member the baby will have wrapped around their little finger first.
Will the baby be an early bird or a night owl? Everyone votes with a thumbs up (early) or down (night).
Guess the first place {names} will take the baby on a proper outing.
Predict the baby's first hobby at age ten. Go around the room — no repeats allowed!
Guess which nursery rhyme will become the baby's absolute favourite.
Which will come first: first tooth, first crawl, or first real giggle? Everyone picks one.
Would you rather change a diaper blindfolded or sing every instruction out loud for a whole day?
Would you rather have a baby who sleeps all night but wakes at 5am, or one who sleeps until 8 but wakes twice?
Would you rather assemble a crib with no instructions or a stroller with instructions in a language you don't speak?
Would you rather have a toddler who only speaks in questions or one who only speaks in song?
Would you rather name the baby's first pet or pick the baby's first Halloween costume?
Would you rather read the same picture book 40 times in a row or sing the same song 40 times in a row?
Would you rather have a baby who laughs at everything or a baby who dances to everything?
Would you rather be the fun aunt/uncle who visits once a month or the reliable one who babysits every Tuesday?
Tell the room about the first time you ever held a newborn. Be honest about the nerves!
Share your favourite story about {name} that the baby should hear one day.
What's a funny thing you did as a toddler that your family still talks about?
Describe {names} in three words. Then explain the least obvious one.
Tell the story of how you first met {name}. Everyone else gets one follow-up question.
What's a family tradition you hope this baby grows up with? Tell us where it came from.
Share a moment you saw {name} being caring before they were a parent-to-be.
What was your favourite toy as a child, and what happened to it?
You have 30 seconds to list as many baby animal names as you can (kitten, calf…). Go!
Invent a brand-new lullaby line on the spot and sing it. The room scores it out of 10.
Mime a new parent's morning routine. First person to guess the step you're on takes the next card.
Name five things in this room that would need baby-proofing. Clock's ticking — 20 seconds!
Explain how to swaddle a baby using only your hands — no words. Someone narrates for you.
Come up with a silly middle name suggestion for the baby that rhymes with the day of the week.
In 20 seconds, name as many children's books as you can remember — titles or just the plot.
Do your best impression of a baby tasting a lemon for the first time. The room votes on accuracy.
On three, point at the guest most likely to become the baby's favourite babysitter.
Point at who will send the most baby photos to the group chat. Most pointed-at reads the next card.
Who in the room would win a diaper-changing speed race? Point on three!
Point at the person most likely to spoil the baby with too many toys.
Who here will teach the baby their first silly dance? Point now!
Point at the guest who'll be the calmest in a baby emergency. They get to pick the next player.
Who's most likely to cry happy tears when they first meet the baby? Point on three.
Point at the person who'll invent the baby's first nickname.
Quick-fire: name a baby animal for every letter of the alphabet, going around the room. Stumble and you're out!
Quick-fire: go around the room naming things you pack in a diaper bag. First repeat or pause is out.
Quick-fire: name a lullaby, nursery rhyme or kids' song. No repeats — last one standing wins.
Quick-fire: say a word to describe {names} as parents. Keep going until someone blanks.
Quick-fire: name a first — first steps, first word, first haircut… Go round until nobody can think of one.
Quick-fire: name a sound a baby makes. Performance encouraged.
Raise your glass (any drink!) and make a one-sentence wish for the baby's first year.
Toast {names}: finish the sentence "This baby is lucky because…"
Make a toast to the grandparents-to-be and the village that's about to help.
Give a toast to {name}'s patience, future sleep, and sense of humour. In that order.
Toast the baby's future best friend, whoever they turn out to be.
Whisper-free round: what's the kindest thing a stranger ever said to you about parenting (or being a kid)?
Guess the baby's future bedtime-story request: dragons, dinosaurs, space, or the sea? Everyone picks.
If the baby could have one superpower from someone in this room, whose would it be and why?
